input_signals.name: Leverage-Weighted Profitability Inflection
input_signals.expression: MUL(SUB(IND_RANK(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at), 3)), IND_RANK(NEG(TREND(RATIO(SUB(SUB(revt, cogs), xsga), at), 3)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(ADD(dltt, dlc), at)))
input_signals.hypothesis: Sustained operating-profitability improvement predicts higher returns, and deterioration predicts lower returns, with both effects amplified by leverage.
input_signals.reasoning: The signed profitability trend replaces the FF5-like profitability level, while continuous leverage weighting makes the tails compare improving and deteriorating highly leveraged firms. Unlike a leverage gate, the expression retains cross-sectional variation for all firms and directly estimates how debt pressure changes the value of profitability inflections.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( sub( ind_rank( trend( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), at ), 3 ) ), ind_rank( neg( trend( ratio( sub( sub( revt, cogs ), xsga ), at ), 3 ) ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( add( dltt, dlc ), at ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating Recovery with Balance-Sheet Repair
input_signals.hypothesis: Operating turnarounds followed by simultaneous reductions in net liability pressure predict higher returns because balance-sheet repair confirms that the recovery is economically substantive.
input_signals.reasoning: The minimum operator makes the weaker of operating improvement and net-liability reduction the binding signal, preventing either standalone effect from dominating. Both components are continuous and broadly available, avoiding reliance on the sparse negative-equity population while focusing on coordinated recovery dynamics.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: min( ind_rank( delta( ratio( oiadp, at ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( sub( lt, che ), at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Interest Rollover Squeeze
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms earn lower subsequent returns when interest expense strains operating cash earnings while short-term debt represents a large share of total liabilities.
input_signals.reasoning: Interest expense minus EBITDA measures a continuous fixed-charge shortfall that remains economically ordered even when EBITDA is negative. Multiplication by short-term debt concentration isolates the interaction between inadequate operating coverage and imminent refinancing pressure rather than a generic leverage effect.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( xint, oibdp ), at ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dlc, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Capital Burden Cash Depletion
input_signals.hypothesis: A capital-consumption burden exceeding EBITDA predicts lower returns when cash reserves are simultaneously being depleted.
input_signals.reasoning: This removes interest expense and debt-maturity concentration, replacing the prior rollover mechanism with realized liquidity erosion under capital-replacement pressure. Cash depletion confirms that the depreciation-versus-EBITDA shortfall is becoming financially consequential rather than merely identifying capital-intensive firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( dp, oibdp ), at ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( che, at ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Supplier-Credit Margin Squeeze
input_signals.hypothesis: Heavy reliance on non-debt current liabilities predicts lower returns when thin gross margins leave little capacity to satisfy suppliers and other operating creditors.
input_signals.reasoning: Current liabilities net of short-term debt proxy operating-credit dependence rather than conventional financial leverage. Interacting that dependence with cost-of-goods intensity distinguishes productive supplier financing from operating obligations supported by inadequate gross margins.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( ratio( sub( lct, dlc ), revt ) ), ind_rank( ratio( cogs, revt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Rollover Asset-Productivity Deficit
input_signals.hypothesis: Low revenue productivity predicts lower returns when short-term debt is concentrated because the asset base generates insufficient operating scale for imminent refinancing needs.
input_signals.reasoning: Industry-adjusted asset turnover replaces the nearly collinear historical profitability maximum with an operating-efficiency channel not directly captured by FF5 profitability. Current maturity concentration preserves coverage and identifies where low asset productivity is most financially consequential.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( ind_adj( ratio( revt, at ) ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( dlc, lt ) ) )

input_signals.name: Productivity Recovery with Maturity Extension
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms earn higher subsequent returns when industry-adjusted asset productivity improves while short-term debt concentration declines.
input_signals.reasoning: Coordinated operating-efficiency recovery and maturity extension provide mutually reinforcing evidence of substantive rehabilitation rather than a profitability level effect. Both legs are one-period changes, so the signal distinguishes active repair from structurally productive or conservatively financed firms.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( delta( ind_adj( ratio( revt, at ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( dlc, lt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Operating Loss Current-Asset Drawdown
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(oibdp, at)))), IND_RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(act, at), 3), RATIO(act, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Weak operating profitability predicts lower returns when current assets have already fallen substantially from their recent peak.
input_signals.reasoning: The distress channel is depletion of the broader current-asset reserve rather than another cash-level or profitability-drawdown conditioner. Industry adjustment reduces structural profitability differences, while the current-asset drawdown identifies firms that may be liquidating short-horizon resources to sustain operations.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( ind_adj( ratio( oibdp, at ) ) ) ), ind_rank( sub( ts_max( ratio( act, at ), 3 ), ratio( act, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Fixed-Charge Recovery with Maturity Extension
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms earn higher subsequent returns when fixed-charge coverage improves while short-term debt concentration declines.
input_signals.reasoning: The signal captures coordinated repair in both operating debt-service capacity and refinancing structure rather than another current interest-coverage level. Requiring both improvements may preserve the strong interest-pressure mechanism while reducing exposure to firms whose apparent recovery occurs on only one side of the balance sheet.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( sub( xint, oibdp ), at ), 1 ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( dlc, lt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Asset-Productivity Maturity Wall
input_signals.expression: MUL(IND_RANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(revt, at)))), IND_RANK(SUB(RATIO(dlc, lt), TS_MIN(RATIO(dlc, lt), 3))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Low asset productivity predicts lower returns when short-term debt concentration has risen materially above its recent low.
input_signals.reasoning: The maturity leg captures an emerging refinancing wall rather than a structurally high short-debt share. Combining that directional financing state with industry-adjusted productivity should retain the strong monotonic operating-capacity evidence while sharpening the portfolio distress event.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( neg( ind_adj( ratio( revt, at ) ) ) ), ind_rank( sub( ratio( dlc, lt ), ts_min( ratio( dlc, lt ), 3 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Three-Way Refinancing Rehabilitation
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(DELTA(IND_ADJ(RATIO(revt, at)), 1)), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(SUB(xint, oibdp), at), 1)))), IND_RANK(NEG(DELTA(RATIO(dlc, lt), 1))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms earn higher subsequent returns when asset productivity and fixed-charge coverage improve while short-term debt concentration declines.
input_signals.reasoning: The minimum makes operating-scale recovery and servicing-capacity recovery jointly binding before maturity extension is applied. This tests a comprehensive rehabilitation mechanism rather than allowing one favorable accounting change to dominate the signal.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( delta( ind_adj( ratio( revt, at ) ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( sub( xint, oibdp ), at ), 1 ) ) ) ), ind_rank( neg( delta( ratio( dlc, lt ), 1 ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Dual-Capacity Asset-Reserve Depletion
input_signals.expression: MUL(MIN(IND_RANK(NEG(IND_ADJ(RATIO(revt, at)))), IND_RANK(RATIO(SUB(xint, oibdp), at))), IND_RANK(SUB(TS_MAX(RATIO(act, at), 3), RATIO(act, at))))
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms earn lower subsequent returns when both asset productivity and fixed-charge coverage are weak after the current-asset reserve has been depleted.
input_signals.reasoning: Low revenue productivity and an interest shortfall identify distinct operating-scale and debt-service deficiencies, with the weaker rank made binding. A current-asset drawdown adds realized loss of short-term funding capacity rather than another static leverage or profitability level.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( min( ind_rank( neg( ind_adj( ratio( revt, at ) ) ) ), ind_rank( ratio( sub( xint, oibdp ), at ) ) ), ind_rank( sub( ts_max( ratio( act, at ), 3 ), ratio( act, at ) ) ) )

input_signals.name: Margin Recovery with Cash-Coverage Rebuild
input_signals.hypothesis: Firms earn higher subsequent returns when gross margins recover while cash coverage of current liabilities simultaneously improves.
input_signals.reasoning: Margin recovery identifies improving unit economics, while higher cash-to-current-liability coverage confirms that the improvement is translating into immediately usable financial flexibility. This avoids working-capital accrual changes and does not recycle the fixed-charge-and-maturity rehabilitation core.
input_signals.author: proposer
input_signals.normalized_expression: mul( ind_rank( delta( ratio( sub( revt, cogs ), revt ), 1 ) ), ind_rank( delta( ratio( che, lct ), 1 ) ) )
